title: data/sidecars/<slug>.md front matter
description: The only hand-written per-paper input. Targets fidelity -- being described correctly -- not just visibility. One sidecar per paper, ONE owner even when the paper has many authors: two co-authors independently paraphrasing the same finding is the fragmentation problem at scale.

key.description: BibTeX key, for cross-checking against papers.yaml.

coined.description: The coined name, if any: TIES-Merging, ZipNN, DOVE.

gloss.description: Plain-language phrase for the coined name. Rendered adjacent to it everywhere, because a coined name has no lexical path from the question people actually ask.

one_liner.description: The canonical sentence. Reused VERBATIM in the page, README, model card, and talk abstract -- rewording fragments corroboration.

qa.description: Question groups. Never a question without its answer adjacent: a question-only passage matches the query and then loses the citation, because the concrete answer is not in the chunk.

ask.description: ONE question, asked by four different kinds of person. Fill `plain` always and at least one other: each role is a different lexical route to the same answer, and engines fan a query into synthetic sub-queries you cannot predict, so three vocabularies beat three rewordings of one. Every role is a natural question ending in `?`, never a keyword string.

plain.description: The question as someone who has NOT read the paper would type it: no jargon, no coined name, names its own subject.

jargon.description: The same question in the field's own vocabulary, the way a specialist would type it.

task.description: The same question phrased as the thing they are trying to do -- 'how do I merge two adapters without retraining'.

practitioner.description: The same question in the first person, deciding -- 'should I use this for my model'. This is the highest-intent phrasing and the one a person asks an assistant.

unsorted.description: LEGACY ONLY -- phrasings written before the roles existed. Never emit this field: put every phrasing in the role it belongs to.

answered_by.description: Claim ids, never prose. The renderer emits each claim's text verbatim. Never paraphrase a claim: a restated claim is a second, drifting version of your own finding.

kind.description: What the claim asserts, which decides what else it owes. `result` (the default when absent) is something the paper measured or demonstrated, and must cite `evidence`. `context` is what the paper IS -- what it contributed, what problem it opened, where it sits in its literature -- and needs no evidence, because a paper contains no sentence certifying its own standing. The asymmetry is deliberate: the highest-volume questions an engine receives ('what should I read about model merging') have no answer in any result claim, so a page of only result claims is invisible to them. `scope` is what makes the unverified half safe, which is why it stays required on both.

text.description: Self-contained and quotable: names the object, the finding and the magnitude in one sentence. No pronoun pointing outside the sentence -- it will be retrieved alone.

scope.description: The conditions under which it holds and does not. This is content, not a disclaimer. Boilerplate ('further research is needed') is worthless. LLM summaries drop scope ~5x more often than humans do; this is the only lever on that. On a `context` claim it carries more weight still: it is the entire bound on a claim nothing in the paper verifies.

evidence.description: Where in the paper: 'Table 2', 'Figure 4b'. Required on a `result` claim, absent on most `context` ones.

misreadings.description: What people wrongly conclude from this paper. Stated as corrections, not as questions.

terminology.description: Terms of art used in a non-obvious sense in THIS paper.

links_extra.description: What cannot be derived from identifiers: project page, talk video, slides, poster, leaderboard, blog post, demo. Merged into the derived links map.
